beats.narration_text: Block or Detect?

shot.visual_intent: Act title arrives and holds

beats.narration_text: People often use collider to mean a solid boundary, and trigger to mean an overlap sensor. Both use collision geometry. In Godot, the owning physics body or area determines the role. The same rectangle can stop a character or report its passage.

lecture.runner_up: A static table cannot demonstrate blocking versus passage
lecture.why: A spatial comparison makes the behavioral difference visible before code

shot.visual_intent: Collider and trigger are roles
shot.motion_claim: Move matched actors toward equal rectangles; stop one, pass the other, mark an entry event

show.event: Move matched actors toward equal rectangles; stop one, pass the other, mark an entry event

beats.narration_text: Collision Shape Two D supplies geometry. Put it under a physics body to participate in that body's collision behavior. Put it under Area Two D to define a sensor region. The three D equivalents follow the same separation.

lecture.about: Geometry does not choose the role
lecture.runner_up: A screenshot of unrelated Inspector settings would obscure ownership
lecture.why: The actual door tree shows both ownership arrangements together

beats.narration_text: Here is an actual scripted Godot experiment. Two identical character shapes receive the same movement requests. The upper rectangle belongs to a static body. The lower one belongs to an area. Predict which character stops, and which produces overlap events.

lecture.runner_up: Conceptual motion is reserved for the preceding mechanism
lecture.why: The engine output anchors the prediction in a runnable setup

beats.narration_text: The upper character stopped at the solid boundary. The lower character crossed the area, producing one entry and one exit. The geometry was the same size. This result tests this setup; it is not a guarantee about every speed or shape.

lecture.why: Actual captured outcome closes the prediction loop

beats.narration_text: The player lives on layer three, whose bit value is four. The door sensor has no membership layer in this example, but its mask includes the player. A sensor can detect a target without the target scanning the sensor in return.

lecture.runner_up: A matrix is useful for larger policies, but this is one directed query
lecture.why: Real settings connect the directed query to named layer numbers

shot.visual_intent: Reveal the player layer and the approach mask from the executed source

props.title: sensor-mask · source excerpt
props.code:
[node name="Approach" type="Area2D" parent="."]
collision_layer = 0
collision_mask = 4
[node name="CollisionShape2D" type="CollisionShape2D" parent="Approach"]
shape = SubResource("SensorShape")

beats.narration_text: Our coin detected the player even though the player did not scan pickups. Removing the area's mask prevented detection. That is a directed area query. Do not turn it into a universal rule that every body pair needs reciprocal masks.

lecture.why: Verbatim recorded output establishes the observation and keeps its evidence limits visible.

beats.narration_text: Monitoring asks whether this area detects overlaps. Monitorable asks whether other monitoring areas can detect this area. Our tests disable each independently. For the monitorable test, we move the target out and back before checking the new overlap.

lecture.runner_up: An untested property list would invite the common reversal
lecture.why: Recorded tests distinguish the observer setting from the target setting

beats.narration_text: Body entered and body exited report physics bodies. Area entered and area exited report other areas. Our door listens for bodies because the player is a character body. A weapon area hitting a hurtbox area needs the area signals instead.

lecture.about: Choose the event for the target
lecture.runner_up: A broad signal catalog would distract from the target type
lecture.why: The real door script explains the selected API without inventing a weapon implementation

beats.narration_text: Overlap lists are updated during physics processing. Moving an object and immediately reading a cached list can show the previous result. Prefer enter and exit signals for transitions. In an automated experiment, wait for the relevant physics steps before asserting the outcome.

lecture.about: Overlap results belong to physics updates
lecture.runner_up: A static property reference cannot show temporal ordering
lecture.why: A labeled sequence makes timing and stale reads explicit

beats.narration_text: Physics overlap callbacks can run while queries are being flushed. Defer changes such as disabling a shape or monitoring. The coin sets a synchronous claimed flag first, then schedules the physics change and emits its value.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

beats.narration_text: An entry is an event. Occupancy is state. Store each entering actor by instance identifier and erase it on exit. Weak references let this door discard actors that were freed. A dictionary also avoids mistaking one actor's exit for an empty room.

lecture.runner_up: A single boolean demonstration would hide multiple-actor limitations
lecture.why: Executed door logic connects edge events to persistent occupancy

shot.visual_intent: Reveal insertion, erasure and stale-reference cleanup

beats.narration_text: There is no body stay signal in this interface. For a damage zone, enter and exit can maintain a target set, while a timer applies damage at a chosen interval. Decide whether damage happens immediately on entry and how cooldowns work.

lecture.runner_up: A code listing would imply a tested damage system we have not built
lecture.why: A constructed timeline distinguishes event frequency from game policy

shot.visual_intent: Continuous effects need a policy
shot.motion_claim: Mark one enter, several deliberate timer pulses while occupied, then exit stops pulses

show.event: Mark one enter, several deliberate timer pulses while occupied, then exit stops pulses

beats.narration_text: A falling player above an enemy can suggest a stomp, but comparing origins alone is a heuristic. Feet-aligned pivots help interpretation. A top sensor or contact-normal test, plus side and corner tests, makes the intended rule clearer.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

shot.visual_intent: Stomp or hurt
shot.motion_claim: Contrast a top approach with a side approach at similar heights; keep the heuristic boundary visible.

show.event: Contrast a top approach with a side approach at similar heights; keep the heuristic boundary visible.

beats.narration_text: This example uses a separate top sensor for a falling player's stomp. A side sensor requests damage. The defeated latch prevents repeated events, and sensor changes are deferred. Simultaneous corner contacts still need an explicit priority policy.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

beats.narration_text: This door has a narrow solid panel inside a larger approach sensor. The sensor can notice the player before the player reaches the panel. Detection requests an interaction; it does not automatically authorize opening. The locked setting remains a separate gameplay rule.

lecture.runner_up: A conceptual door illustration would lose the tested geometry
lecture.why: Actual engine capture shows both regions in one reusable scene

shot.visual_intent: Focus on the outer approach region, then the narrow blocking panel
shot.motion_claim: Focus on the outer approach region, then the narrow blocking panel

show.event: Focus on the outer approach region, then the narrow blocking panel

beats.narration_text: The open method first checks the lock and the open-state guard. It then disables only the solid shape, using a deferred change. The approach area remains active. Removing the entire door would also remove the sensor and its occupancy information.

lecture.about: Open the panel, keep the sensor
lecture.runner_up: A before-and-after picture alone hides the deferred mutation
lecture.why: Executed implementation shows exactly what changes

shot.visual_intent: Reveal guards before the deferred shape mutation

beats.narration_text: The test verifies that a locked door refuses opening, an open door keeps its sensor, and an occupied door refuses closure. After the actor exits, closing restores the solid shape. Multiple actors arriving during closure still deserve a separate stress test.

lecture.about: Close only when the region is clear
lecture.runner_up: A door animation would not establish the guards
lecture.why: Actual assertions establish scope and leave concurrency limits visible

beats.narration_text: An area can also influence local gravity or damping; it still does not act as a solid wall. A rigid body can report contacts too when configured. Choose geometry, physical response, event reporting, and gameplay state as separate decisions.

lecture.runner_up: A fabricated gravity demonstration would overstate the available evidence
lecture.why: The tested pickup grounds the role; API extensions are identified in narration

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. For CSYE seventy-two seventy, Building Virtual Environments. A solid boundary blocks while a trigger detects overlap. Masks and monitoring settings determine sensor detection. Transition events need explicit gameplay state and timing. A door combines a solid panel with an independent sensor.
